description:
Downstream consumers that pattern-match agent output (the agent-observer use case) need to work against the *rendered* screen, not the raw PTY byte stream — ANSI escapes, cursor moves, and redraws make regexes brittle and false-positive-prone.

Despite the package name, internal/vterm/ is session/fan-out management, not a terminal emulator. Each consumer currently has to wire its own vt100 parser (vt10x, tcell, etc.) on top of attach.Run.

Proposed shape (small, optional):

  package screen

  type Screen interface {
      // Feed raw PTY bytes (as delivered by attach output).
      Write(p []byte) (int, error)

      // Snapshot the current rendered grid.
      Cells() [][]Cell      // or whatever the chosen lib exposes naturally
      Text() string         // plain-text flattening, newline per row
      Cursor() (col, row int)
      Size() (cols, rows int)
  }

  func New(cols, rows int) Screen   // wraps a vt100 emulator (likely vt10x)

Consumer flow:

  scr := screen.New(80, 24)
  // in the attach output goroutine:
  scr.Write(buf[:n])
  // periodically / on signal:
  if strings.Contains(scr.Text(), "Waiting for input") { ... }

Scope:
- Wrap one existing emulator (vt10x is the obvious pick); do not roll our own.
- No resize coordination — caller passes the geometry they care about.
- No event hooks / pattern engine — that's the consumer's concern; this package only provides the rendered view.

Out of scope:
- Headless screenshotting / image rendering.
- Diff streams between snapshots (consumers can diff Text() themselves).

Depends on ship-y2s — pkg/ only exists as a public layout once that ticket decides whether to move or re-export. File this as a follow-up once the public API shape lands.

Lower priority than the API exposure work; defer until a second observer-style consumer materializes if the first one ships fine with its own vt10x glue.
title: pkg/screen: rendered-screen view of a mosey PTY stream
